issue.title: Untrusted-content provenance: contract spec for prompt-injection defense
issue.body:
Parent: #270

## Why

Indirect prompt injection via repository content (README, code comments, issue text) into coding agents is OWASP's #1 LLM threat (340% YoY growth) and has been demonstrated against Claude Code-style agents via malicious GitHub repos. Factory ingests untrusted brownfield repos (RFC-0010) and GitHub issue text (RFC-0011) by design, and has no injection threat model today. RFC-0012 already gives us the fail-closed gate pattern to extend.

## Implementation steps

1. Write a short threat-model doc (`docs/security/untrusted-content-threat-model.md`): enumerate untrusted inputs per service - issue/spec text at PFactory intake, cloned repo content at AIFactory coder, target-repo content at TFactory verify, MCP server responses fleet-wide.
2. Add `$defs.provenance.content_trust` to `apis/task-contract.schema.json`: mark spec/issue-derived text as `untrusted_user_content` vs. operator-authored `trusted`; carried through all handoffs.
3. Specify the fail-closed rule (RFC-0012 pattern): if a scan gate (see AIFactory child) flags likely injection payloads, the task pauses to human_review rather than proceeding - never silent-continue.
4. Specify prompt-hardening requirements for services: untrusted content must be delimited/quoted in prompts with an explicit "data, not instructions" framing; document the canonical wrapper in the RFC-0003 governed-integration doc.
5. Define the completion-event field for scan verdicts so CFactory can display them (injection_scan: pass/flagged/skipped + reason).

## Acceptance criteria

- Threat-model doc merged.
- Contract PR merged with content_trust marking (optional, backwards compatible).
- Scan-verdict field defined in the completion-event envelope spec (minor version bump).

## Consuming children

- PFactory: intake marking. AIFactory: pre-coder scan gate. CFactory: verdict surfacing.

279.title: docs(security): untrusted-content threat model + content_trust + injection_scan (#273)
279.body:
## What

Spec-only prompt-injection defense contract for the fleet (parent epic #270). No service code.

- **Threat model**: `docs/security/untrusted-content-threat-model.md` — untrusted inputs per service (PFactory intake issue/spec text, AIFactory cloned-repo content, TFactory target-repo/verify output, MCP responses fleet-wide), the fail-closed rule (flagged => pause to human_review, skipped never reported as pass), and the canonical untrusted-content prompt delimiter services must adopt verbatim.
- **Contract**: `apis/task-contract.schema.json` — new optional `$defs.content_trust` referenced from the inline `provenance` block (`default: trusted | untrusted_user_content` + per-origin `sources[]`). Backwards compatible; absent => consumers assume `untrusted_user_content` (fail-closed default). Diff kept tightly scoped to the provenance block and the new $defs entry to avoid conflicts with the concurrent $defs.routing work.
- **Completion-event envelope**: RFC-0001 new §3.2 + `apis/completion-events.asyncapi.yaml` — additive optional `injection_scan` block (`verdict: pass | flagged | skipped`, `reason` required for flagged/skipped, optional `scanner`/`sources_scanned`). Minor version bump to 1.3 (1.2 was the CloudEvents upgrade already described in RFC-0001 §3).
- **RFC-0003**: one design principle cross-referencing the canonical wrapper for GitHub-ingested text (issue step 4).

## Why

Indirect prompt injection via repo/issue content is OWASP's #1 LLM threat, and the Factory ingests untrusted brownfield repos (RFC-0010) and GitHub issue text (RFC-0011) by design. This defines the marking, the gate semantics, and the surfacing field the PFactory/AIFactory/CFactory children of #270 will implement.

## Verification

- `python scripts/validate_task_contract.py` — OK (schema still a valid 2020-12 JSON Schema).
- New `content_trust` block exercised with jsonschema: absent OK, well-formed OK, bad enum rejected, source item missing `trust` rejected.
- AsyncAPI YAML parses (yq); contract JSON parses.

Closes #273

Generated with Claude Code (https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Pull request overview Defines a spec-only, fleet-wide contract for handling untrusted content to mitigate indirect prompt injection, including provenance marking (`content_trust`), a fail-closed scan gate semantic, and surfacing scan verdicts via the completion-event envelope. **Changes:** - Adds an untrusted-content threat model document with a canonical prompt wrapper and fail-closed gate rules. - Extends the task-contract schema with optional `provenance.content_trust` for trust marking across handoffs. - Adds the optional `injection_scan` block to the completion-event RFC and AsyncAPI contract (minor version bump to 1.3). ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | docs/security/untrusted-content-threat-model.md | New threat model + canonical delimiter + fail-closed scan semantics. | | docs/rfc/0003-github-agentic-integration.md | Adds a GitHub-ingested-text handling principle referencing the threat model. | | docs/rfc/0001-correlation-key-and-completion-event.md | Defines the optional `injection_scan` envelope block (v1.3). | | apis/task-contract.schema.json | Adds `provenance.content_trust` and introduces the `$defs.content_trust` schema. | | apis/completion-events.asyncapi.yaml | Adds `InjectionScan` schema and exposes `injection_scan` on the event. |
